svg.title: Fig. 33(b) — The ellipse as a section of a cone: two spheres, PF1 + PF2 = AB
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 33(b), page 38. Section: conics.

g.data-text: The right circular cone with vertex V, cut by a plane that meets all its generators on one side of V: the curve of intersection is an ellipse.

Inscribe two spheres in the cone, one on each side of the cutting plane, both touching it: at F1 (small sphere) and F2 (large sphere). Their circles of contact with the cone lie in two parallel planes (hatched).
Take P on the curve and draw the generator VP. It touches the small sphere at A and the large sphere at B. The tangents from P to a sphere are equal: PF1 = PA and PF2 = PB.

PF1 = PA, PF2 = PB, so PF1 + PF2 = AB: the distance between the two circles of contact measured along a generator. It is a constant (the same for every P), so the curve is an ellipse with foci F1, F2.
